body.heading: What experience hides
paragraphs: Experience is valuable, but it has a side effect: you stop seeing the thing itself and see your habits instead. The experienced cook stops tasting, the experienced writer stops hearing the sentence, because the routine runs itself.
A beginner's mind is the deliberate opposite: looking at the familiar as if for the first time, with permission to not know and to ask obvious questions.

body.heading: Practise seeing freshly
paragraphs: Take something you know well and describe it to an imaginary complete beginner, in plain words, without jargon. The places where you stumble are the places your understanding was running on habit.

Or borrow real beginners: teach a newcomer, answer a child's questions, try the left-handed version. Their fresh eyes will show you your own craft from the outside, which is a view experts rarely get.

takeaway: Look at one familiar thing as if for the first time, and notice what habit was hiding.
